summary: Single deployable monolith: React Native (Expo) (Android) on Python 3.13 + Django 5.2 LTS with Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 17, hosted on Google Cloud Run — asia-south1 (Mumbai), at an estimated $13-66/month.

frontend.justification: Team already writes javascript for the mobile app; mature on-device storage and background sync; good fast delivery (priority 4/5); good low running cost (priority 5/5). Low-end devices: React Native (Expo) adds a JavaScript runtime, so keep the bundle small, use the default Hermes engine, lazy-load screens and profile memory on a 2 GB phone; Kotlin + Jetpack Compose (native Android) is the fallback if memory is tight, though it ranks lower here: team lists javascript, python but this needs kotlin/java (team.languages=javascript,python); with priorities.time_to_market=4, React Native is faster to deliver with.

alternatives.why_not: Team lists javascript, python but this needs kotlin/java (team.languages=javascript,python); with priorities.time_to_market=4, React Native is faster to deliver with.
Heavier runtime on low-end phones (project.description); with priorities.performance=3, React Native is faster at runtime. Known limit of Ionic Capacitor: WebView performance on low-end devices.

tradeoffs: JS runtime overhead on very low-end phones
frontend.contrast: React Native (Expo) (Android) rather than Kotlin + Jetpack Compose (native Android). Team lists javascript, python but this needs kotlin/java (team.languages=javascript,python); with priorities.time_to_market=4, React Native is faster to deliver with. Trade-off accepted: JS runtime overhead on very low-end phones.

backend.justification: Team already writes python for the API; good low running cost (priority 5/5); good maintainability (priority 4/5).

alternatives.why_not: With priorities.time_to_market=4 and priorities.security=3, Python 3.13 + Django 5.2 LTS is faster to deliver with and stronger on security. Known limit of Node.js 24 LTS + NestJS: more boilerplate than Express.

With priorities.maintainability=4 and priorities.time_to_market=4, Python 3.13 + Django 5.2 LTS is easier to maintain and faster to deliver with. Known limit of Python 3.13 + FastAPI: bring-your-own admin/auth pieces.

pareto.note: No eligible option rates at least as well on all six priorities (cost, delivery, scalability, performance, maintainability, security).

confidence.label: medium
confidence.basis: stability 0.87 (moderate) over 54 priority vectors; score margin 1.8 over the runner-up.

backend.contrast: Python 3.13 + Django 5.2 LTS rather than Node.js 24 LTS + NestJS (TypeScript). With priorities.time_to_market=4 and priorities.security=3, Python 3.13 + Django 5.2 LTS is faster to deliver with and stronger on security. Trade-off accepted: WebSockets need Django Channels.

database.justification: Handles write-heavy load; good low running cost (priority 5/5); good maintainability (priority 4/5). GPS coordinates are stored as PostGIS geography points, so area and distance queries run in the database.

alternatives.why_not: With priorities.maintainability=4 and priorities.security=3, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 17 is easier to maintain and stronger on security. Known limit of Cloud SQL for MySQL 8.4: 8.0 moved to Sustaining Support (Apr 2026); no row-level security.

With priorities.cost=5 and priorities.maintainability=4, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 17 is cheaper to run and easier to maintain. Known limit of Supabase Postgres: free projects pause after 1 week of inactivity; production needs Pro.

tradeoffs: Vertical write scaling; sharding needs extensions

confidence.label: high
confidence.basis: stability 1.00 (robust) over 54 priority vectors; score margin 5.6 over the runner-up.

database.contrast: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 17 rather than Cloud SQL for MySQL 8.4. With priorities.maintainability=4 and priorities.security=3, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 17 is easier to maintain and stronger on security. Trade-off accepted: Vertical write scaling; sharding needs extensions.

hosting.justification: Satisfies the hard constraints (managed_cloud (no servers to patch), data_residency india -> asia-south1 (Mumbai)). Scales out with requests for traffic bursts and back down (to zero) afterwards, so idle periods cost little; fully managed runtime (patching, TLS, scaling handled) for a team without a DevOps person; good low running cost (priority 5/5); good maintainability (priority 4/5).

alternatives.why_not: With priorities.cost=5, Google Cloud Run is cheaper to run; it fits better: scales out with requests for traffic bursts and back down (to zero) afterwards, so idle periods cost little (scale.traffic_pattern=spiky).
With priorities.cost=5, Google Cloud Run is cheaper to run; operations burden 2/5 with no dedicated DevOps person (team.has_devops=false).

tradeoffs: Cold starts unless min instances are paid for

supporting.justification: phone_otp for Indian users: an Indian SMS provider with DLT-registered templates is the cheapest reliable OTP route (about Rs 0.20 per SMS); the backend stores users and refresh tokens in the in-region database.

alternatives.why_not: stores identity data in Google's global auth service, conflicting with India residency
about $0.05 per verification plus SMS, far above Indian SMS rates

tradeoffs: DLT registration of sender ID/template before launch
OTP needs network at login; sessions must stay valid offline

supporting.justification: Uploads (GPS-tagged photos) go straight from clients to object storage via signed URLs. Private bucket, server-generated signed URLs, encryption with managed keys.

alternatives.why_not: with ~100 GB of data expected in 12 months (scale.data_volume_gb_12_months), files inside the database bloat every backup and cost more per GB than object storage
zero egress fees, but a second vendor outside GCP

supporting.choice: Google Cloud Pub/Sub / Cloud Tasks in asia-south1 (Mumbai)
supporting.justification: Background work: photo post-processing (thumbnails, EXIF/GPS extraction) after bursts of offline syncs.

alternatives.why_not: slow responses and lost work when a call fails

supporting.justification: Automated tests and deploys on every push to Google Cloud Run; free minutes cover a team of 2.

alternatives.why_not: equally capable; for a team of 2 without a DevOps engineer (team.has_devops=false), ready-made GitHub deploy actions for Google Cloud Run mean less pipeline code to maintain

tradeoffs: Secrets must be stored as encrypted environment secrets

supporting.choice: Cloud Logging + Cloud Monitoring in asia-south1 (Mumbai)
supporting.justification: Logs and metrics stay with the host provider in asia-south1 (Mumbai); alerts on error rate and latency.

alternatives.why_not: stores data only in the US or EU

tradeoffs: Log retention costs grow with traffic

supporting.choice: Offline-first sync: expo-sqlite + background task, outbox + idempotent sync API
supporting.justification: Must work without connectivity: writes go to an on-device database first; an outbox queue retries uploads when signal returns; each record carries a client-generated UUID so retries are idempotent; server applies last-writer-wins per field with an edit log; photos are compressed on-device and uploaded with resumable chunks; sync batches are small and compressed for 2G/3G.

alternatives.why_not: convenient but ties data to Google's global service and its pricing

tradeoffs: Conflict resolution rules must be agreed with field teams
Device storage limits on low-end phones

assumptions: Hosting Google Cloud Run: $0-10/month at the 'tiny' tier.

Database Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 17: $10-30/month. Assumes a shared-core instance (db-f1-micro to db-g1-small: $0.0126-0.042/hour in Mumbai, $0.0105-0.035 in Iowa, about $8-31/month, Google pricing page 11 Nov 2026). Google excludes shared-core instances from the Cloud SQL SLA and advises against production use; a dedicated-core instance costs more.
queue: Google Cloud Pub/Sub / Cloud Tasks in asia-south1 (Mumbai) $0-1/month.
observability: Cloud Logging + Cloud Monitoring in asia-south1 (Mumbai) $0-5/month.

Stored data ~100 GB after 12 months at ~$0.02-0.035/GB-month: $2-5/month (year-end volume used as an upper bound, not an average); bulk files and media are assumed to sit in object storage, while database rows stay small.
Phone OTP: 2,000 users x 0.3-1.0 OTP logins/month at India SMS ~Rs 0.20-0.25 + GST per SMS = $1-9/month (long-lived sessions keep OTPs rare).
Spiky traffic: the upper bound is a peak month; with autoscaling, quiet months run near the lower bound.
Excluded: taxes, domain names, paid support plans and data-egress spikes. Order-of-magnitude band, not a quote.

warnings.message: Phone OTP needs signal at first login; sessions are long-lived refresh tokens so the app keeps working offline afterwards.

DPDP Act 2023: collect consent with a clear notice, support access/correction/erasure requests, keep a breach runbook (the DPDP Rules 2025 require prompt intimation to the Board and affected people, then a detailed report within 72 hours; the Rules commence in phases, so confirm which apply on your launch date) and delete data when the purpose ends. Hosting in India simplifies transfers; legal review still required.

assumptions: requirements.p95_latency_ms absent or null: no explicit latency target; typical web latency assumed.
Knowledge base as of 2026-11-11; lifecycle and pricing judgements use that date, not the run date.
Scale tier 'tiny' from 2,000 users and ~200 peak concurrent users (people, not requests per second; used only for sizing and cost).
